form.label: Migration Reality — Simple XML (synthetic)
form.description: A synthetic Splunk Simple XML dashboard modeled on the SHAPE of real customer log-analysis dashboards (time + search-backed dropdown fieldset, rows of mixed panels). All field/index names are invented. Run through the SPL->NRQL importer, it shows what actually happens on a migration: a little works, much breaks. Panel titles label the category; the importer's placeholder panels self-document the original SPL and the reason.

chart.title: CLEAN: timechart over a real field (renders)
RENDER-FAIL live: top -> ORDER BY (passes console, red-banners in widget)
LOSSY: time-picker token $tr.earliest$ dropped — panel loses its time window

search.query: earliest=$tr.earliest$ latest=$tr.latest$ index=web_logs status>=500 \ | timechart count by status

chart.title: GAP: wildcard rename (log.* as *) — common in K8s log dashboards

search.query: index=k8s_logs | rename log.* as * | stats count by level
index=web_logs | rex field=_raw "user_id=(?<uid>\w+)" | stats count by uid
index=web_logs | iplocation clientip | stats count by Country
index=web_logs | mvexpand tags | stats count by tags

chart.title: GAP: strftime time bucketing in eval

search.query: search * | eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H") | stats count by hour
index=web_logs | transaction session_id maxpause=30m | stats count

chart.title: GAP: affixed token pod="*checkout-$env$-api*" (token inside a literal)

search.query: index=k8s_logs pod="*checkout-$env$-api*" | stats count by level

html.p: In Splunk this is a free-text panel. The importer turns every <html> panel into a placeholder — so even your documentation panels need re-authoring.
